title: Limiting Reagent Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A fire dies with wood still left, a sandwich stall runs out of cheese, and a bicycle shop runs short of wheels. In each case one thing runs out first and decides how much you can make. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 1, Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry) we find that limit in any reaction.

You will see what the limiting reagent and the excess reagent are, using seven frames and ten wheels. On the molecule bench, two nitrogen molecules meet three hydrogen molecules: the hydrogen is used up making two ammonia molecules, and one nitrogen molecule is left over. We build a four step method, compare two cases to show why you compare moles and never grams, then solve the NCERT example (50.0 kg N2 and 10.0 kg H2, hydrogen limiting, about 56 kg of ammonia). An extra practice numerical with methane (clearly marked as practice, not NCERT), the exam trap of comparing moles without the coefficients, an original NEET pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself close the lesson.

This is Episode 13 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 Three shortages, one idea
0:29 Limiting and excess reagent
0:50 Molecule bench: not enough hydrogen
1:27 The four step method
1:49 Two cases + pause and think
2:32 NCERT worked example: 50 kg N2, 10 kg H2
3:25 Practice numerical: methane and oxygen
4:01 Exam trap: divide by the coefficient
4:28 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:10 Recap and three questions to answer
